prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right one depends on your budget, health needs, whether you want ACA/subsidized coverage or a private/short‑term plan, preferred doctors, and how much hand‑holding you want. I can help you find a good match, but here’s a practical approach and what to look for in Kansas City, MO.

How to find a good broker
- Use local, independent brokers who work with multiple carriers (not captive agents tied to one insurer). They can compare plans side‑by‑side.  
- Search the NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) agent directory or the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance licensed agent lookup to verify licenses and complaints.  
- For ACA plans, look for agents certified as Marketplace (Healthcare.gov) navigators or certified agents — they can enroll you in plans and help with subsidies. Missouri uses the federal Marketplace (Healthcare.gov).  
- Consider reputable national online brokers (e.g., eHealth, GoHealth) if you prefer fast quotes, but an in‑person/local broker may better handle income/profit complexities for self‑employed people.

What to ask any broker before you hire them
- Do you specialize in individual/ACA plans and self‑employed clients? (Experience with subsidy calculations and quarterly income changes matters.)  
- Which carriers do you represent? Can you show several comparable plan options?  
- How are you paid — commission only, fees, or both? Any extra fees I should expect?  
- Will you help with Marketplace subsidy estimates and year‑end reconciliation? (Important for self‑employed)  
- Will you assist with claims or problems after enrollment? Is ongoing support included?  
- Can you provide references or online reviews from clients?

Specific issues for self‑employed people
- Subsidy estimates are based on projected Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI). A good broker will help you project income and explain reconciliation at tax time.  
- If your income fluctuates, ask about mid‑year plan changes and Special Enrollment options.  
- If you have a small business with employees, ask about SHOP plans or association plans — different rules apply.

Where to look locally
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance: verify licensing and complaints.  
- NAHU agent locator for Kansas City area agents.  
- Healthcare.gov’s “local help” finder for certified agents/navigators near you.

If you want, I can:
- Search and shortlist 3–5 Kansas City brokers who specialize in individual/ACA plans and serve self‑employed clients (I’ll need your ZIP code and whether you prefer in‑person or remote help).  
- Draft a short script/email you can send to brokers to compare them quickly.

Which would you prefer: a shortlist of local brokers (give ZIP) or the comparison script/questions to use?
